heading: The route, before step 1
lede: Seven stages, thirty-nine steps, one browser. Roughly twenty minutes with the figures in front of you.

stages.title: Set the job up
stages.caption: Year, name, how you count income — and the stock question, which is the one that bites.

stages.title: Money coming in
stages.caption: Lines 1 and 2. Check the income total before you type twenty expense lines.

stages.title: Money going out
stages.caption: Part II line by line, the mileage and meals helpers, and the list of anything else.

stages.title: Home and van
stages.caption: The home office, then the vehicle questions — which only exist because line 9 has a figure.

stages.title: Check, then produce
stages.caption: Read the panel, pick cents or whole dollars, download the PDF and the spreadsheet.

stages.title: Keep it and check it
stages.caption: Save a draft, open both files and read them, then clear the machine if it is not yours.

stages.title: Prove it yourself
stages.caption: Pull the network out and do it again. It still works — that is the privacy claim, checked.

notes.then: Part III appears — six inventory lines. Untick it and they go, but anything typed in them stays in your figures.
A whole section of vehicle questions appears further down, with your miles already in it.
A panel that was hidden until now appears at the foot of the page. Never before the file.
It is refused where you typed it, the profit above quietly leaves it out, and both download buttons go dead.
